upsert.title: Experimental silver nanoparticle treatment for canine and feline cancer
upsert.center: Hospital Veterinario Peña Jasso / UNAM-UABC-UAG translational nanomedicine project
upsert.contacts: Enrollment is through Hospital Veterinario Peña Jasso in Ensenada, Baja California. Owners first register and the hospital performs a clinical evaluation to determine suitability for the experimental phase.
upsert.notes: Current 2026 translational program CBF-2025-G-82 led by Dr. Nina Bogdanchikova. A fresh recruitment report quotes the project veterinary collaborator directly: dogs and cats with a cancer diagnosis may be considered after individualized clinical review; 16 veterinary patients had already been treated at the time of reporting. Owners pay for pre-enrollment evaluation tests; once admitted, consultations, radiographs and follow-up studies are covered by the program. The experimental formulation uses PVP-stabilized silver nanoparticles developed through UNAM-associated research. UNAM's official academic/patent database independently confirms the underlying silver-nanoparticle anticancer composition and inventor team. Evidence of current veterinary recruitment is a direct investigator/collaborator statement in a 2026 news report rather than a dedicated institutional trial registry page, so final eligibility and continued enrollment must be confirmed with the hospital. Do not describe efficacy as established; this remains experimental translational treatment.
